newsitem.title: INDIA: India Oct 95 dollar sales 27.8 bln rupees - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India Oct 95 dollar sales 27.8 bln rupees - RBI.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had sold dollars valued at 27.8 billion rupees in October 1995 when it intervened to prop up the Indian rupee, it said in its annual report for 1995/96 (July-June) released on Friday.

The RBI had intervened in the market last year, selling dollars to stem a steep fall of the rupee against the dollar. Analysts said this is the first time the central bank revealed the extent of intervention.
The rupee fell to a low of 35.65 per dollar in October 1995 from around 31.37 in early 1995.
In November 1995, foreign exchange intervention led to a withdrawal of 3.92 billion rupees from the banking system.
January 1996 saw a bout of sharp fall in the rupee value. In the first week of February 1996, the rupee touched a record low of 37.95 per dollar in the spot market, RBI said.
Net sales of foreign exchange in January 1996 were 14.26 billion rupees and 11.98 billion in February.
Cumulative net purchases of foreign exchange over a nine-month period from October 1995 were 14.01 billion rupees, the RBI said.
